name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-empty-response-retry
description: Makes an unattributed model attempt retryable, for the one seam that can tell. Three reports, one missing evidence. Discussion #8321: a `dsh-llm-pi-ai` route that relays an upstream empty response ends the turn, because `classifyPiAiError` has no rule matching the wording, so the text falls to the catch-all `PI_AI_ERROR`, and that is the one code `DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_CODES` does not carry (`EMPTY_RESPONSE`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `SERVER`, `TIMEOUT`, `TRANSPORT`) — `dsh-llm-retry` short-circuits on `!policy.retryableCodes.includes(failure.code)` and the step is never repeated, though the same adapter maps a locally detected zero-content completion to the retryable `EMPTY_RESPONSE`, so two paths that both mean "the model produced nothing" disagree. This plugin observes the public `llm/stream` waterfall — the one seam that sees an attempt and everything it produced — and rewrites that finish's `failure.code` to the by-value `EMPTY_RESPONSE` when the attempt ended in an unnamed error AND produced nothing at all; the retry executor then accepts the step on its own unchanged code gate. It is strictly narrower than the `retryableCodes: [..., PI_AI_ERROR]` workaround in the report, which widens every catch-all failure on a route: the two producers the adapter marks deliberately non-retryable (`pending`, `deferred` — a not-yet answer is not the safe repeat the principle is about) are excluded, as is any attempt that emitted a block, a token, or a Tool call, and any failure the adapter did name. Nothing buffered, nothing reordered, one boolean of state. 0.2.0 covers the same missing evidence from the other side of the classifier (discussion #9352): a gateway answered 400 with an EMPTY body, the HTTP client surfaced its own sentence for that (400 status code (no body) — the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs share APIError.makeMessage), and classifyPiAiError's rule for the number matched the status inside the client's own sentence, so the turn was reported as INVALID_REQUEST — a name for the one word the client managed to write, not for anything that happened. That code is in no retryable table and no recovery path watches it (compaction keys on CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED alone), so every later turn re-sent the same transcript and failed at step 1: a twelve-minute provider blip bricked the session. The plugin now widens a second recognition, `statusOnlyCodes` (default INVALID_REQUEST), gated on the message by `statusOnlyMessages` being nothing but the client's own bodyless status line — a 400 that carries the provider's words is a diagnosis and is left exactly as it is. 0.3.0 acts on the finding behind the third report (discussion #9397), where a gateway's upstream-retry buffer limit (exceeded request buffer limit while retrying upstream — a 507 with no status number) fell to the catch-all and ended the turn. The observation generalizes: pi-ai decides retryability from a table of its own (RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN — 49 alternatives at 0.87.1, 55 at 1.1.0, measured by test/packaging.spec.mjs against the installed package), and the adapter's classifyPiAiError is a second, partial transcription of it — 24 of the reporter's 49 alternatives are wordings the chain cannot place. So a third recognition reads the same table on the way out: a failure whose code is in `transientCodes` and whose message matches `transientMessages` (the server-shaped half of pi-ai's own table) is rewritten to `transientTargetCode` (default SERVER, the name the chain would have written had it seen the digits), after `vetoMessages` declines pi-ai's NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN first, exactly as pi-ai itself does. Unlike the first two recognitions it needs no produced-nothing condition, because the code is about the route, not about output — dsh-llm-retry gates on retryableCodes.includes(code) alone. 0.4.0 acts on the fourth report (discussion #9402), where a model intermittently streamed a Tool call whose arguments never became JSON: dsh-llm-deepseek validates every assembled call at message_stop and, on the first it cannot read, throws an LlmError with MALFORMED_RESPONSE — a code the adapter chose deliberately, for a refusal about serialization rather than about the request, and one that appears in no retryable table, so the attempt was terminal and the turn ended with nothing durable on it. This is the only recognition whose code the adapter did choose, so it is the only one that must argue from what the attempt assembled rather than from the code alone: unparseableCallCodes (default MALFORMED_RESPONSE) admits the code, and the shape gate then requires that at least one Tool call was assembled, that every one of them is unreadable to the adapter (JSON.parse, then a plain record — its object() helper refuses null, an array, a string and a number as firmly as it refuses a syntax error), and that no text or reasoning arrived beside them. A MALFORMED_RESPONSE that never assembled a call, one beside a readable call, and one after a text delta are all left with the adapter's own code. The raw bytes are not lost by declining to look further: the attempt is recorded before the failure, so the corrupt JSON stays durable in assistant/attempt.stream. 0.5.0 does not change a single rewrite; it changes what the package can *prove* about them. The three supported lines do not run the same pi-ai: the 0.1.6 and 0.1.7 lines resolve 0.85.1 and the 0.2.0-rc line resolves 0.87.1, and the two tables differ by exactly two alternatives (0.87.x adds `currently experiencing high demand` and a bare `520`). The shipped transient defaults and the gaplessness floor had been derived from 0.87.1, so the two oldest lines could not re-derive one default and failed one floor — two arms of packaging.spec.mjs asking a question that was only ever answered about the newest line. A third arm failed for an unrelated reason: the fixture that wires the installed adapter named the credential hook the way only the newest line reads it (resolveAuth, returning headers), while the two oldest lines still call it resolveApiKey, returning the key — so the adapter's credential resolver was undefined, the turn died inside the transport wrapper as TRANSPORT, one layer above the MALFORMED_RESPONSE refusal that suite is about, and every arm gated on measuring that refusal went quiet rather than failing loudly. This release splits the default into the wordings every supported line's table carries and NEWER_LINE_TRANSIENT_MESSAGES (the entry upstream added at 0.87.0, kept in the runtime default and now named as the one place the rewrite is wider than an older line's own table), makes the wording arms assert provenance per installed line instead of against a literal version, and lowers the gap floor to the smallest gap across the supported lines (23, at 0.85.1). The pinned-adapter arm no longer compares a manifest field to a version written in the test file: it asserts that the adapter npm installed *is* the one the manifest pins, which is the invariant a probe that rewrites the manifest for each line still satisfies — and the skip message now names the build actually under test. All three lines pass `npm run test:probe-lines`.
